problem:
A body of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons. At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=\frac{1}{3}{t}^{4}-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}$ meters.

Calculate the time ${t}_{∗}$ at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude. Do not round the answer.

${t}_{∗}=$

{{field-1}} $\text{s}$

feedback.problem:
A body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t\ge 0$ seconds, the velocity of the body is given by $v(t)=4{t}^{2}-32t+64$ meters per second.

Calculate the time ${t}_{∗}$ at which the force acting on the body has zero magnitude. Do not round the answer.

${t}_{∗}=$

{{field-1}}  $\text{s}$
feedback.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

 
where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration. 

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}-32t+64) \\  & =8t-32\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}8t-32 & =0 \\ 8t & =32 \\ t & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at ${t}_{∗}=4\,\text{s}.$
